newsitem.title: VIETNAM: ADB chief urges Vietnam to speed aid disbursement.
newsitem.headline: ADB chief urges Vietnam to speed aid disbursement.

text.p: Asia Development Bank (ADB) president Mitsuo Sato said on Monday that Vietnam needed to do more to speed disbursement of loans from international donors.
Sato said at a news conference in Hanoi that a number of constraints and issues were hampering project implementation in Vietnam, the largest recipient of the Bank's concessional loans.

"These relate to systemic issues such as the need for decentralisation, as well as the technical aspects -- for example the need for efficiency in procurement operations and provision of counterpart funds," he said in a statement.

Sato added that the ADB would be making "utmost efforts" to persuade Vietnam to speed disbursement rates and said that without doing so, Vietnam would risk a loss of confidence among international donors.

"Through the joint efforts of the government and the bank, we hope to achieve a target disbursement ratio in Vietnam of 15 percent by end 1997," he said, adding that the ratio stood at around five percent now.

The ADB resumed lending operations in Vietnam in 1993. As of May this year more than $1 billion has been provided to 15 loans in sectors including agriculture, natural resources, infrastructure, finance and banking.
The Bank proposed in March a $1.5 billion-development programme for the period 1997-2000. The terms included repayment over 40 years with a 10-year grace period and a service charge of one percent.

But it warned in a report a month later that while Vietnam looks set to continue along a path of rapid economic growth over the next two years, it would have to tackle several new problems to ensure social cohesion.
The report said there was reason for concern over a widening of the savings-investment gap, an erosion of social services and growing rural-urban disparities.
Vietnam's communist government launched reforms along market lines in the late 1980s. Despite a subsequent economic takeoff, it remains one of the world's poorest countries.
International donors have pledged some $8.4 billion in aid since 1993. The ADB is Vietnam's fourth largest donor.
